newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australia's shale oil twins up project costs.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australia's shale oil twins up project costs.

text.p: Shale oil hopefuls Southern Pacific Petroleum NL and Central Pacific Minerals Nl said on Friday they have raised the development costs estimates for the Stuart shale oil project in central Queensland.
The two companies known as the "Rundle Twins" said the revised estimate for stage one of the development was now A$250 million which is 15 percent above the orginal estimate.

They said the higher costs were due to revised construction costs and after adding allowances for mining capital, working capital, owners costs, commissioning contingencies and other relatable items the estimated cost of Stuart Stage I.
The Stuart Shale project is being developed jointly between the Rundle Twins and Canada's Suncor Inc.
They said stage one of the project is the first of three planned stages. Initially the co-venturers propose to construct a plant to produce 4,500 barrels per day.

It is planned, following the successful operation of Stage 1, that subsequent stages could raise production progressively to a total of 85,000 barrels per day with the prospect of additional production thereafter, they said.
The co-venturers are in the final stage of negotiating an Engineering Procurement and Construction contract, they said.
At 10.15 a.m. (2315 GMT), both Southern Pacific and Central Minerals shares were 10 cents up at A$4.00 and A$9.20 respectively.
